title: Evaluating Real-Time Voice Agents: From Component Quality to Grounded Outcomes
title_zh: 评估实时语音代理：从组件质量到有依据的结果
abstract_en: Real-time voice agents have moved from research prototypes to production deployments, yet the literature describing them is fragmented across three communities that rarely cite one another: speech foundation modelling, turn-taking psycholinguistics, and agentic evaluation. Architecture papers report latency, turn-taking papers report prediction accuracy, and agentic benchmarks report task success, so no single number describes whether a deployed agent is actually good. We address that gap with three evidence-based claims, each traceable to a corpus of 38 primary sources organised into an application-centric taxonomy of six categories. First, architecture choice is a deployment constraint rather than a settled verdict: a 2026 enterprise tutorial reports that no fully self-hostable end-to-end system yet meets production constraints, while a chunked cascade independently reaches state-of-the-art duplex behaviour, showing duplex behaviour is separable from duplex architecture. Second, evaluation has shifted decisively from component quality toward grounded outcomes, with recent benchmarks verifying backend state rather than trusting what the agent claims to have done. Third, the dyadic assumption in most models and benchmarks is breaking down: multiparty turn-taking and multi-speaker reasoning benchmarks show that deciding when not to speak, and reasoning about who may be told what, are first-class capabilities two-participant framings cannot measure. For each source we state the problem it targets, its mechanism, and its reported evidence, alongside the search strategy, inclusion criteria, and a verification step that caught a misattributed arXiv identifier in circulation. We propose TRG (Timing-Recovery-Grounded), a reporting standard characterising an agent by timing, post-disruption recovery, and state-verified outcome together, with a conditional fourth axis for multiparty deployments.
abstract_zh: 实时语音代理已从研究原型走向生产部署，但相关评估分散在语音基础模型、轮次交替心理语言学和智能体评测三个彼此割裂的社区中，分别关注延迟、轮次预测准确率和任务成功率，缺乏统一标准。本文基于38篇一手文献，构建面向应用的六类分类体系，并提出三项结论：第一，架构选择是部署约束，而非已经定论的优劣判断；端到端架构尚未普遍满足生产约束，而分块级联架构也能实现先进的双工行为，说明双工能力与双工架构可以分离。第二，评估重点正从组件质量转向有依据的结果，近期基准开始验证后端状态，而非仅相信代理的口头声明。第三，多方交互正在突破传统二人对话假设，代理需要具备判断何时不发言，以及根据听众身份决定可透露信息的能力。基于此，本文提出TRG（Timing-Recovery-Grounded）报告标准，从交互时序、受干扰后的恢复能力和状态验证结果三个维度描述语音代理，并为多方部署增加可选的第四维度。
key_points_zh: 实时语音代理的优劣不能由单一指标概括，应同时考察延迟、轮次交互和任务结果。
架构并不存在普适性结论：端到端与分块级联系统都可能实现良好的双工行为，部署约束才是关键。
评估趋势已从语音组件质量转向有依据的任务结果，重点验证后端真实状态，而非代理的自我陈述。
传统二人对话范式不足以覆盖多方场景；判断何时不说话及面向不同听众控制信息披露应成为核心能力。
TRG标准以Timing、Recovery和Grounded outcome为核心，并为多方部署提供额外评估维度。

llm_assessment.comment: This synthesis identifies fragmented evaluation practices in realtime voice agents and proposes a useful standard centered on timing, recovery, grounded outcomes, and multiparty behavior.
llm_assessment.comment_zh: 该综述指出实时语音智能体评测的碎片化问题，并提出围绕时序、恢复、状态验证结果及多人交互的实用报告标准。
